source-8efb486855404b8e.title: SomaSmart independent marking guide
source-8efb486855404b8e.provenance: Worked answers and point-by-point guidance prepared by SomaSmart. Part maxima follow the marks printed in this paper.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Mathematics studies quantities, structures, patterns and relationships through reasoning. It includes measurements, geometry and algebra, in addition to calculations involving money.
parts.rubric: One mark for a clear definition, one for scope beyond money, and one for a suitable example.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Science uses measurement and graphs to describe experiments. Geography uses scales and coordinates to measure distances and locate places.
parts.rubric: One mark per correct subject link and one for a relevant supporting example.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: For example, budgeting, measuring ingredients, estimating travel time and comparing prices.
parts.rubric: One mark per distinct valid reason.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: 3/4 and 1/5 are rational. The total is 15/20 + 4/20 = 19/20.
parts.rubric: One mark for recognising the fractions as rational, one for a common denominator and one for the total.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: √5 and π are irrational. Neither is the quotient of two integers with a nonzero denominator. √5 is the square root of a non-square integer.
parts.rubric: One mark for each named irrational number and one for the correct explanation.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: All four are real. √16 = 4, so −3 + 0 + 4.5 + 4 = 5.5.
parts.rubric: One mark for identifying all the real numbers, one for √16, one for the working and one for 5.5.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Let p be the price of a pen in TZS and n the number bought. Then 0 < p < 500 and np ≤ 2000. Four pens are affordable at any qualifying price. The largest affordable quantity is ⌊2000/p⌋ and depends on p.
parts.rubric: One mark for the strict price inequality, one for the budget relation and one for explaining the quantity or giving the four-pen guarantee. Accept an equivalent interpretation supported by working.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: No. |−7| = 7 because distance from zero is nonnegative.
parts.rubric: One mark for rejecting the claim, one for 7 and one for a valid explanation.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: 5x − 10 = 15 or 5x − 10 = −15, giving x = 5 or x = −1. Both make the expression’s magnitude 15.
parts.rubric: One mark for each case set up, one for both roots and one for interpreting or checking them.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: 88 km.
parts.rubric: One mark for using the tenths digit to decide and one for the rounded value.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Nearest thousand: 175,000 TZS. Nearest hundred: 175,000 TZS.
parts.rubric: Two marks per result, including a correct explanation or rounding step.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: 38.2 rounds to 40 and 41.9 rounds to 40. Estimated total: 80.
parts.rubric: One mark per rounding, one for addition and one for the correct estimate.

parts.label: a
parts.rubric: Identify the first three significant digits, use the next digit and state the rounded value with units, one mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.rubric: Ignore the leading zeroes, use the third significant digit to decide and give the result with units, one mark each.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: 3.415 + 0.00879 = 3.42379, which is 3.42 to three significant figures.
parts.rubric: Two marks for the sum, one for selecting the first three significant digits and one for 3.42.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Eight ratio parts. The girls account for 5/8 × 40 = 25.
parts.rubric: One mark for eight parts, one for the girls’ share and one for 25.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Sand is 20 × 3/2 = 30 kg.
parts.rubric: One mark for the ratio, one for substitution and one for the result with units.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: Speed is 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/h. Distance in five hours is 60 × 5 = 300 km.
parts.rubric: One mark for the speed relation, one for 60 km/h, one for multiplying by five and one for 300 km.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: x + 3 fruits.
parts.rubric: One mark for each quantity and one for using addition.

parts.label: b
parts.rubric: One mark per correct expansion and one for collecting terms.

parts.label: c
parts.rubric: One each for substitution, the square, the product and the correct sum.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: 2x + 3 years.
parts.rubric: One mark for doubling x, one for adding three and one for correctly expressing the age.

parts.label: b
parts.rubric: One mark for adding five to both sides, one for dividing by three and one for the result.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: Let the number be n. Then n + 2n = 18, so 3n = 18 and n = 6.
parts.rubric: One mark each for defining the variable, forming the equation, simplifying and solving.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Let p be the price of a pencil and b the price of a pen. 2p + b = 1500 and p + 2b = 2000.
parts.rubric: One mark for the definitions and one per correct equation.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: b = 1500 − 2p. Substitute to get p + 3000 − 4p = 2000, hence p = 1000/3 and b = 2500/3.
parts.rubric: One mark for isolating b, one for substitution and one for each price.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: A pencil costs 1000/3 TZS (about 333.33 TZS). A pen costs 2500/3 TZS (about 833.33 TZS). The exact values satisfy both totals.
parts.rubric: One mark for each contextual interpretation and one for checking or explaining rounding.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: On labelled x and y axes, place A at (2, 3) and B at (4, 7).
parts.rubric: One mark for suitable axes and scale and one per correctly plotted point.

parts.label: b
parts.rubric: One mark each for the slope relation, substitution and result.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: y − 3 = 2(x − 2), so y = 2x − 1. Both points satisfy it.
parts.rubric: One mark for using the slope, one for substituting a point, one for the equation and one for a check or valid working.

source-889faaee681eeb5f.title: SomaSmart independent marking guide
source-889faaee681eeb5f.provenance: SomaSmart prepared the answers and partial-credit rubric. The paper gives ten marks for each question. Subpart allocations are SomaSmart practice allocations.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Mathematics is the study of quantities, shapes, patterns and relationships through logical reasoning.
parts.rubric: Award up to four marks for an accurate definition, accepting equivalent wording. Credit an example that clarifies the definition.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Examples: manage spending with a budget, measure quantities for cooking or construction, and estimate travel time from distance and speed.
parts.rubric: Two marks per distinct valid application with an explanation, or one per valid application named without explanation.

parts.label: Whole question
parts.answer: Physics: calculate speed as distance divided by time. Geography: use a map scale to find distances. Business Studies: subtract costs from sales to obtain profit. Chemistry: measure the mass of chemicals. Biology: count organisms in samples and compare their frequencies.
parts.rubric: Two marks per distinct subject correctly linked to mathematics with an example. Accept other accurate examples.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Draw a scaled number line and mark the point at positive 5, five units to the right of zero.
parts.rubric: Two marks for the consistent scale, one for locating zero and two for correctly marking and labelling 5.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Divide the distance between 3 and 4 into four equal parts and mark the third division after 3, at 3¾.
parts.rubric: One mark for each labelled endpoint, one for four equal intervals and two for the correct marked point.

parts.label: Whole question
parts.answer: x = 1/3 and y = 2/3. Therefore y² = 4/9, while x² + x = 1/9 + 1/3 = 4/9. The two sides are equal.
parts.rubric: Two marks per correct conversion, two for the left side, three for the right side and one for the conclusion.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Mark −3 and 5 with filled circles and draw the segment between them.
parts.rubric: One per correctly placed endpoint, one per filled circle and one for the segment.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Mark 2 and 5¼ with open circles and draw the segment between them.
parts.rubric: One per correctly placed endpoint, one per open circle and one for the segment.

parts.label: Whole question
parts.answer: For w weeks, 500,000 − 40,000w ≥ 200,000, so w ≤ 7.5. She can make seven full weekly withdrawals. Seven leave 220,000 TZS, while eight leave 180,000 TZS.
parts.rubric: Three marks for the budget inequality, two for isolating w, one for 7.5, two for the whole-week answer and two for a valid interpretation or check.

parts.label: Whole question
parts.answer: x − 2 ≤ −4 or x − 2 ≥ 4. Hence x ≤ −2 or x ≥ 6, including both endpoints.
parts.rubric: Four marks for the two branches, four for the two solution bounds and two for including both boundaries in the final answer.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Approximation gives a value close to an exact quantity, usually by rounding to a useful level of precision.
parts.rubric: Two marks for closeness to the exact value, one for expressing the idea of estimation or rounding and one for a valid example or precision explanation.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: For example, estimate the cost of shopping before paying and estimate travel time from distance and average speed.
parts.rubric: Three marks per distinct valid use with explanation or an example. Accept other plausible uses.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: 8.74. The third decimal digit is 5, so the hundredths digit increases from 3 to 4 under the usual school rounding rule.
parts.rubric: Two marks for identifying the hundredths and next digit, one for the rounding decision and two for the result.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: 9,340,000. The ten-thousands digit is 3 and the thousands digit is 5, so round up and replace the lower digits with zeroes.
parts.rubric: Two marks for locating the relevant digits, one for the rounding decision and two for the result.

parts.label: Whole question
parts.answer: 15,248,412 + 18,450,356 = 33,698,768. To the nearest ten thousand, the result is 33,700,000 people.
parts.rubric: Four marks for the correct total, two for identifying the rounding place and deciding to round up, and four for the final rounded population, including the carry.

source-817d378b48f73ba6.title: SomaSmart independent Physics marking guide
source-817d378b48f73ba6.provenance: SomaSmart worked answers for selected questions. The paper supplies the maximum marks shown for each part.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Examples include a lever, pulley, inclined plane and wheel and axle. A wedge or screw is also valid.
parts.rubric: Award one mark for each of four distinct types.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.answer: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 225 N ÷ 75 N = 3.
parts.rubric: Award one mark each for the relationship, substitution and correct result.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.answer: Efficiency = (mechanical advantage ÷ velocity ratio) × 100% = (3 ÷ 4) × 100% = 75%.
parts.rubric: Award one mark each for the relationship, substitution and percentage.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: A cell or low-voltage supply, switch, resistor, ammeter and voltmeter. Connecting leads complete the circuit. A variable resistor allows several readings to be taken.
parts.rubric: Award one mark each for five distinct suitable components.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Draw a closed series loop with a low-voltage supply, switch, ammeter and test resistor. Draw the voltmeter across the test resistor. A variable resistor may go in series to adjust the current.
parts.rubric: Award one mark each for the supply, closed series path with switch, test resistor, ammeter in series and voltmeter across the resistor.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: The ammeter goes in series to measure the current through the resistor. The voltmeter goes in parallel across the resistor to measure potential difference across it. For DC meters, match their polarity to the circuit and select appropriate ranges.
parts.rubric: Award two marks for the ammeter connection with its reason, two for the voltmeter connection with its reason and one for an appropriate meter precaution.
